summary: Iter 263 backend-only regression testing for KOLOR Studio email cleanup. 5/5 pytest tests passed: login baseline, GET /api/calendar/events (200), GET /api/calendar/google-events with no connection (200 {connected:false, events:[]} — verifies handleCalendarAuthFailure wiring did not break the happy-path), POST /api/leads/submit (201, public, sendAutoResponse + sendClientConfirmation + sendInquiryAcknowledgementEmail non-blocking), POST /api/leads (201, auth, sendAutoResponse call site). Backend booted cleanly — no import errors from the 2 deleted email functions (sendContractReminderToClient, sendDiscoveryCallInviteToClient). Grep confirmed zero remaining references to deleted functions. sendCalendarDisconnectedAlert (email.ts:3287) and sendAutoResponseEmail (email.ts:1537) both present.

minor.issue: Non-blocking Resend 403 'validation_error' in backend.err.log — RESEND_API_KEY is set but domain not verified, so Resend restricts to owner email (emmanuelobokoh03@gmail.com). Routes still 201 correctly because email sends are fire-and-forget with .catch() handlers. NOT a regression from iter 263 — pre-existing env constraint.
Slow response ~1361ms flagged by [Perf] middleware. Uses 5 parallel Prisma queries — pre-existing, not touched by iter 263.

critical_code_review_comments: handleCalendarAuthFailure (calendar.ts:11-29) — clean implementation: deletes CalendarConnection first (natural once-only debounce via short-circuit at connection lookup), then fire-and-forget email with error catch. Good pattern.

google-events route (calendar.ts:325-378): invalid_grant detection uses String(refreshError?.message).includes('invalid_grant') which is fragile against SDK message changes; googleapis typically throws with err.response.data.error === 'invalid_grant'. Consider also checking that structured field. Minor — non-blocking.

google-events error handler catches error?.code === 401 || 403 — but googleapis errors may have .code as string or number, or the status may live at error.response.status. Consider normalizing: const code = error?.code ?? error?.response?.status. Minor — non-blocking.
leads.ts POST /submit at line 461: still hardcodes fallback owner email 'emmanuelobokoh03@gmail.com' — should be env-driven (DEFAULT_OWNER_EMAIL). Pre-existing, out of iter 263 scope.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_-prefixed leads via /api/leads/submit (public inquiry, cannot delete without auth as different user; will remain in DB) and /api/leads (auth, cleaned up via DELETE in fixture).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login endpoint (POST /api/auth/login) returns {message, user} and sets an HttpOnly JWT cookie — there is no token in the JSON body. Use requests.Session() to preserve the cookie for subsequent auth-required calls. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_iter263_email_cleanup.py demonstrates the pattern. RESEND_API_KEY is set in this env but Resend is in test/unverified-domain mode — expect 403 validation_error in logs for any /api/leads/submit or /api/leads POST; this is expected and does NOT affect route status codes (routes still return 201).
